cohort: 5,275 Australian women aged 18-38 years who had given birth to their first child between 1996 and 2012
finding: Australia has a high caesarean section rate (29.1% for first births), with higher maternal age, BMI, short stature, anxiety, and private health insurance being predictive factors for caesarean section in first births.
mod_finding: Vaginal birth after caesarean section was more common in women who were older, short-statured, or had been overweight or obese for both children, compared to women who had two vaginal deliveries.
